newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van Ommeren raises ROE target to 15 pct. [CORRECTED 12:35 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Van Ommeren raises ROE target to 15 pct. [CORRECTED 12:35 GMT]

text.p: Dutch shipping and tank storage company Koninklijke van Ommeren said on Thursday it had raised its return-on-equity target, to be reached by the year 2000, to 15 percent.

"Our gradual refocus on services with higher added value has enabled us to raise the return on equity target we set several years ago from 12 percent to 15 percent, to be attained by around the year 2000," chairman Carel van den Driest told a news conference on Van Ommeren's 1996 results.
He said chemicals and gas transport and storage were two sectors with healthy margin prospects.
The company declined, however, to give any firm forecast for its full year result in 1997.

"The year has only just started and it is really too early to give anything firm...The dollar seems to be favouring us, but maybe that is just for now," Van den Driest said. (Corrects to remove erroneous reference to dollar being weak.)
Earlier, Van Ommeren posted 1996 net profit of 94.4 million guilders, up from 1995's 80.3 million. The dividend was raised to 2.50 guilders per share from 2.00 in 1995.
